heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Overture PETG straight out of the box with its stock hardened steel nozzle, achieving reliable print speeds up to 167 mm/s based on a conservative 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. While the printer is fully enclosed, opening the top glass or front door is recommended to avoid heat creep during prolonged runs.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with thin layer of glue stick or liquid release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high Bambu speeds.
Calibrate Pressure Advance (PA) in OrcaSlicer, setting the starting K-value around 0.035 to 0.042 for direct drive PETG.
Disable nozzle clumping detection or lift the top glass slightly to prevent chamber temperatures exceeding 40°C during long prints.
Enable Z-hop on retraction (0.2 mm spiral or auto) and set travel speed to 400 mm/s to minimize filament stringing across open cavities.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Fine stringing and cobwebbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Overture PETG is hygroscopic and tends to ooze when saturated with atmospheric moisture, aggravated by excess travel heat.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament in a dehydrator or X1C bed at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or permanently bonding to smooth bed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically bonds aggressively to smooth PEI coatings, ripping the coating off upon part removal.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to the Bambu Textured PEI plate and apply a thin layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue as a sacrificial release layer.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Over-extrusion at the nozzle tip during wall transitions combined with high printing temperature causing material dragging.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce Flow Ratio in OrcaSlicer by 2-3% (typically around 0.94-0.96) and lower nozzle temperature to 238°C.

faq.question: Should I print Overture PETG with the Bambu Lab X1C door closed?
faq.answer: It is best to leave the door cracked or the top glass vented. An enclosed chamber can exceed the glass transition temperature of PETG (approx. 70°C bed heat soaking the chamber), causing softening in the extruder and heat creep clogs.

faq.question: What volumetric flow limit should I configure in OrcaSlicer for this filament?
faq.answer: Set your Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s. Pushing standard Overture PETG beyond 14 mm³/s in a standard 0.4mm nozzle will cause severe under-extrusion and dull matte surface banding.

faq.question: Do I need to dry Overture PETG brand new out of the vacuum bag?
faq.answer: Yes. Even factory-sealed spools of Overture PETG frequently contain ambient moisture from the manufacturing water-cooling bath; drying at 65°C for 6 hours eliminates foaming and stringing.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu High Temp Plate or Cool Plate for PETG?
faq.answer: You can use the High Temp Plate only if you apply a dedicated glue stick barrier to prevent fusing. Never print PETG directly on the Cool Plate as it will tear the sticker.
